source: Server Training Guide: Sales Techniques (David, SWR Hospitality)

cards.prompt: A couple tells you it's their anniversary. How do you adjust your suggestions?
options: Suggest a bottle, and a dessert to share
Keep suggestions quick and practical
Suggest value options and sharing items for the table
Explain the signature dishes
answer: Suggest a bottle, and a dessert to share
cards.explanation: Celebrating guests are open to treating themselves: suggest bottles, premium items, desserts to share and a celebration touch.
cards.why: The right suggestion makes their occasion feel special.

cards.prompt: Two guests at a business lunch keep checking their watches. How do you adjust?
options: Keep suggestions quick; offer coffee to go
Suggest a bottle and a dessert to share
Explain the signature dishes in detail
Suggest a sharing starter while they decide
answer: Keep suggestions quick; offer coffee to go
cards.explanation: Guests checking their watches are short on time, so keep suggestions quick and practical, and offer coffee to go.
cards.why: Respecting their time is the best service you can give.

cards.prompt: A family is reading the prices very carefully. How do you adjust?
options: Suggest value options and sharing items
Suggest premium upgrades as a little treat for them
Don't suggest anything at all
Suggest the specials of the day
answer: Suggest value options and sharing items
cards.explanation: Budget-conscious guests: recommend value options and sharing items, and avoid pushing premium upgrades.
cards.why: Guests who feel their budget is respected relax and enjoy their visit.

cards.prompt: Guests tell you it's their first time at Maison Mathis. What fits best?
options: Explain our signature dishes and house specialities
Mention the new dishes and what's changed since last month
Leave them to explore the menu alone
Suggest the quickest dishes
answer: Explain our signature dishes and house specialities
cards.explanation: First-time visitors are curious and want guidance, so explain the signature dishes and house specialities.
cards.why: A great first visit is how a guest becomes a regular.

cards.prompt: A guest isn't drinking alcohol. What do you do with drinks suggestions?
options: Suggest mocktails and fresh juices as warmly as cocktails
Skip drinks suggestions altogether so they don't feel awkward
Ask them why they're not drinking tonight
Offer water only
answer: Suggest mocktails and fresh juices as warmly as cocktails
cards.explanation: Guests not drinking alcohol still want something special. Recommend mocktails, fresh juices and premium waters with the same enthusiasm, and never make a guest explain.
cards.why: Every guest deserves a great drink, with or without alcohol.

cards.prompt: Regulars know the menu well. What should you suggest to them?
options: New items and specials, and their favourites
Nothing; they already know what they want
The signature dishes, explained in full detail again
The most expensive dish on the menu
answer: New items and specials, and their favourites
cards.explanation: Regulars know the menu, so mention new items and specials, and remember their favourites.
cards.why: Remembering a regular's favourite makes them feel at home.

cards.prompt: What's the golden rule of selling?
options: Sell to the guest's needs, not to your target
Suggest something on every visit to the table
Always offer the premium option first
Focus on the items with the best margin
answer: Sell to the guest's needs, not to your target
cards.explanation: Sell to the guest's needs, not to your target. A guest who feels looked after will return; a guest who feels pushed will not.
cards.why: Long-term, loyal guests are worth far more than one bigger check.

cards.prompt: A guest is showing signs of having had too much to drink. Their glass is empty. What do you do?
options: Don't suggest another drink; follow responsible service rules
Offer a smaller measure or a lighter drink instead of a full one
Suggest a lighter beer, like Hoegaarden
Ask if they'd like the same again
answer: Don't suggest another drink; follow responsible service rules
cards.explanation: Never suggest another round to a guest showing signs of intoxication. Follow responsible service rules and the venue's licensing conditions.
cards.why: Guest safety and our licence come before any sale.

cards.prompt: A guest with a nut allergy asks which dessert you'd recommend. What do you do?
options: Confirm with the kitchen first, then recommend a safe option
Recommend a dessert that has no nuts listed anywhere on the menu
Recommend the Dame Blanche straight away
Say you can't recommend any desserts
answer: Confirm with the kitchen first, then recommend a safe option
cards.explanation: Always check allergies before recommending and confirm with the kitchen if you're unsure. Never guess, then recommend a safe option with genuine enthusiasm.
cards.why: An allergy can be life-threatening, and the menu doesn't show every ingredient.

cards.prompt: Which tables should you offer upgrades to?
options: Any table, respectfully, without assuming
Only the tables that look like they're big spenders
Only tables that are celebrating
Only regulars who know the menu
cards.explanation: Never assume who can or can't afford an upgrade. Offer options respectfully to every table.
cards.why: Judging a guest's budget is the quickest way to lose their trust.

cards.prompt: Before service, what should you check with the kitchen so you don't sell the unavailable?
options: Sold-out (86'd) items and preparation times
The staff meal time
The chef's favourite dish
Tonight's table plan and the reservations list
cards.explanation: Check with the kitchen before service for 86'd (sold-out) items and preparation times.
cards.why: Recommending a dish that's sold out disappoints the guest twice.
